The shape of `opencode run --format json` events is not documented in Buracle's research; these patterns only assume that tool names appear as JSON strings (MCP tools are named <server>_<tool> in OpenCode). Inspect the smoke-run stdout and rewrite the patterns before trusting any result.
usage: Per arm: --env HOME=<arm>/home --env XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<arm>/home/.config --env XDG_DATA_HOME=<arm>/home/.local/share plus provider credentials. Keep --standalone: without it the run attaches to the background service, which carries the user's real configuration. Add --append-arg --auto only for edit cases, with the user's consent.

grader.status: Read-only judge run with OpenCode's plan agent, standalone so it never attaches to the background service. Smoke-graded on opencode 2.0.30 against a local fake Anthropic endpoint (providers.anthropic.settings.baseURL in the throwaway config): the argv is accepted and the answer arrives in a text event. The plan agent still lists the edit tools; its permissions deny them. The quality of a real model's judgment is not covered by that smoke.
grader.usage: Give the grader its own throwaway config like an arm: --env HOME=<root>/grader/home --env XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<root>/grader/home/.config --env XDG_DATA_HOME=<root>/grader/home/.local/share plus credentials. Pin the model: --append-arg --model --append-arg <provider/model>.
